title: Catalog entry: removing a value in use
summary: quality.floor in draft v10 with mp3-320 removed from its allowed values while the Studio profile, 1 license and 4 accounts still use it: an inline warning names them, asks where they move, and Review stays disabled until they have an allowed value.
compare: The removed chip stays in place, dashed and struck, with Undo; the other chips keep their usage tags.

The warning sits directly under the chips, not in a toast or a dialog, and names everyone affected from the U-29 effective read: the Studio profile with how many licenses it covers, each license that sets its own (by holder), and the accounts as a count with Show them.

Move them to lists only the values still allowed (flac, aiff, any). Until one is picked the select is in its error state and the error says what to do: "Choose where they move. Review stays off until everyone on mp3-320 has an allowed value."
Review 2 changes is disabled while anyone would be left on a value that isn't allowed; the same rule holds when the Default's own value is removed (Default must be picked again).
Nothing moves until v10 is published, and the warning says so. The Review step then lists every profile, license and account that moves, with old and new values.
The rail's Studio profile row shows mp3-320 struck with "removed" in warning text.
Phone: the warning's list and picker stack inside the callout; the picker fills the width.
